clue.text: The last word I caught back in multiplex

indicators.note: going back means the assembled string is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: the word said at the close of a prayer
taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone at a crowded multiplex finally catches the last line of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last word' is a fixed phrase for the closing word of a prayer; it and the next two pieces are strung together and then turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: A multiplex is a large building housing several screens, i.e. a kind of picture house showing films.

clue.text: Flower in neat border

blocks.note: neat is an old word for cattle; here read as possessive, cow's
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a flower in a tidy flowerbed edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like 'tidy' but is the archaic word for cattle, so 'neat border' becomes a cow's lip.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow wild primula of meadows, a familiar spring bloom.

clue.text: Having a bad name, there must be no nonsense about debts

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so that word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
rot is rubbish talk; it is turned round
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debt

explanation.surface: A stern creditor warns that someone with a poor reputation must settle their debts without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous for something bad, i.e. carrying an ill reputation.

clue.text: Swallow one cocktail

blocks.note: the martin is a bird of the swallow family
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone downs a single cocktail in one gulp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' reads as a verb about drinking, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a mixed drink of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: US group in a Hitchcock film, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the title is taken by sound only

blocks.note: The Birds is Alfred Hitchcock's 1963 thriller

explanation.surface: An American band appears in a Hitchcock movie, or so rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Byrds were a 1960s American folk-rock band, famous for Mr Tambourine Man.

clue.text: Rockery Daphne cultivated right here in London

indicators.note: cultivated ground is dug over and worked, so these letters are turned over into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A gardener tends a rockery planted with daphne shrubs, right here in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Daphne is a flowering shrub, which suits the gardening picture; the definition is just 'here in London', a place in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde Park Corner is a major junction and landmark at the south-east corner of Hyde Park in London.

clue.text: Wading bird from bitingly cold centre of Afghanistan

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its single middle letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: bitter weather is sharply, painfully cold
the sixth of eleven letters

explanation.surface: A wading bird is spotted far from home in the freezing heart of Afghanistan.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a heron-like marsh bird known for its booming call.

clue.text: Profligate pocketing grand, the villain

indicators.note: to pocket something is to take it inside, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a roué is a debauched, dissolute man
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A wastrel helps himself to a thousand, the scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest scoundrel, a synonym for a villain.

clue.text: Sheet of low cloud in place, round middle of afternoon

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one word wraps the other
the middle of a nine-letter word is its fifth letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: one's place in society is one's status, or standing
the fifth of nine letters

explanation.surface: A forecast: a blanket of low cloud settling in by mid-afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is the meteorological term for a flat, grey layer of cloud at low altitude.

clue.text: Steal connoisseur's comic book

indicators.note: comic suggests something absurd and jumbled, so these letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: to rob is to steal
taken as written; the 's that follows joins it to the indicator

explanation.surface: A thief pinches a collector's prized comic book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic book' looks like one thing; 'comic' is the anagram signal and 'book' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe is Daniel Defoe's 1719 novel about a castaway.

clue.text: After changes in statement leaves Irish town

indicators.note: changes here means the word is altered, its letters reset in a new order
in places the rearranged letters inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
a word can mean a remark or statement, as in 'a word of warning'

explanation.surface: After amendments to a statement, someone departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a departure but just links wordplay to definition, meaning 'gives'.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterford is a city and port in south-east Ireland, famous for crystal.

clue.text: Row involving golf and golfer?

indicators.note: involving means including within, so one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: a tier is a row of seats
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dispute involving golf and a player of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests an argument but is a line of seats; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger Woods is a famous American golfer, so his first name stands for a golfer by example.

clue.text: One good short rule for getting over disease?

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the word loses its final letter
getting over suggests flipping round, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
G is the standard abbreviation for good
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A simple rule of thumb for shaking off an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The lurgy (also lurgi) is a jokey British word for an unspecified illness, made famous by the Goon Show; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The lurgi is a mock name for any vague, catching ailment, so it is a humorous term for sickness.

clue.text: Carry out a tool

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to put a plan into effect
second meaning: a noun, an instrument or utensil

explanation.surface: An instruction to use or remove a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for putting a decision into effect and a noun for a utensil or instrument.

clue.text: IOUs, say, may cause person's morosity

indicators.note: what something may cause is its product, so these letters are made into something new

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Mounting debts can make someone gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: IOUs are an example of written promises to pay a sum, which is what promissory notes are; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Resemble escort behind

blocks.note: to take someone somewhere is to escort them
after means coming behind

explanation.surface: Someone looks like the person accompanying them from the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: To take after a parent is an idiom for looking or behaving like them.

clue.text: Damaged hip concerns king, not young any more

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are broken and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch's injured hip suggests he is getting on in years.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone no spring chicken is an idiom meaning they are past their youth.

clue.text: Name a whale briefly seen round stern of icebreaker?

definitions.text: Name a whale briefly seen round stern of icebreaker?

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter
a ship's stern is its back end, so only the final letter is kept
being seen round something means encircling it, so letters wrap that one

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written
its final letter
whale cut short

explanation.surface: Identify a whale glimpsed briefly around the back of an icebreaker ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a whale sighted near an Arctic icebreaker; the question mark admits it is a description by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhal is a tusked Arctic whale that lives among sea ice, exactly where icebreakers work.

clue.text: Runs round excellent town in New Mexico

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is round in shape
swell is old slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Someone jogs around a fine little town in the American Southwest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs round' looks like a container instruction, but each word gives its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Roswell is a city in New Mexico, famous for the 1947 supposed UFO crash.

clue.text: Resolve shown by golf club abroad

blocks.note: an iron is a type of golf club
out means away or outside, as in abroad

explanation.surface: A golfer's determination is on display at an overseas club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolve' looks like a noun meaning determination, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron out difficulties is an idiom for settling or smoothing away problems.

clue.text: School for young children in northern Surrey refurbished

indicators.note: something refurbished is done up and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
taken as written; Surrey is an English county south of London

explanation.surface: A kindergarten in the north of Surrey has been renovated.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery school takes children below the age of formal schooling.

clue.text: Hospital doctor injecting substance right into bottom

indicators.note: injecting puts something inside, signalling one string goes within another
into confirms where the letters go: inside the following word

blocks.note: the gist is the substance or main point of something
R is the abbreviation for right
rear is a polite word for the buttocks

explanation.surface: A doctor gives a patient a jab right in the backside.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a registrar is a senior doctor in training, below consultant.
explanation.definitionFit: In the UK a registrar is a grade of hospital physician ranking just under a consultant.

clue.text: Cereal crops in ground needing a shower

indicators.note: a crop is the topmost part, so just the head of the next word is taken

blocks.note: its first letter
a shower is a fall of rain

explanation.surface: Crops planted in dry earth need a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cereal crops' reads as one phrase, but 'Cereal' alone is the definition; 'crops' takes the top letter of 'ground'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain is the seed of cereal plants such as wheat or barley, and the collective name for them.

clue.text: Being broadcast in Arizona - Ironside

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the following words, spanning them

blocks.note: the end of the state name and the start of the surname

explanation.surface: An episode of the TV detective series Ironside, set in Arizona, is going out live.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironside was an American TV detective series, which fits 'being broadcast'.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is one currently being transmitted on radio or television.

clue.text: Cast in low spirits, mostly, at the end of revue

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
the end of a word is its last letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: heavy, as in heavy-hearted, cut short
its final letter

explanation.surface: A gloomy theatre cast feels down at the finale of their revue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests the actors in the revue, but it is a verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave something is to throw or hurl it with effort, a synonym of cast in that sense.

clue.text: Study the topography to ascertain the prevailing conditions

blocks.note: first meaning: literally, look at the lie of the terrain
second meaning: the figurative idiom for assessing a situation

explanation.surface: A surveyor examines the terrain to judge what things are like.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means surveying terrain and figuratively means finding out how matters stand before acting.

clue.text: See 24
Lie about closure of dance floor

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other
the closure of a word is where it ends, so only its last letter is kept

blocks.note: a story is a fib or untruth
its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone fibs about why the dance floor was shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance floor' reads as one thing, but 'floor' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is a level of a building, which is what a floor means in that sense.
